cases.why: The three-part form with a TYPE LIBRARY in the first slot, which is the form the addressability task is really about - `[[Lib.]Enum.]Value`. Measured separately from the module-qualified form because they are different mechanisms: a module is a project member, a library is a referenced type library, and HexIDE models them as different QualifierKinds. Raised by a maintainer citing this exact expression.

The same shape against the VBA library rather than VBRUN. Included because the two libraries are referenced differently by a Standard EXE and need not behave alike, and because a rule that holds for only one of them is not a rule.
The two-part form for a LIBRARY enum - enum name without the library. If this works and the three-part does too, the library slot is optional in exactly the way the [[Lib.]Enum.] notation suggests.

The bare form for a library enum member. Predicting legal - these constants are used bare in every VB6 program ever written - and included as the control that proves the other three are about qualification rather than about the name existing.

Library-qualified but skipping the enum level. Decides whether the middle slot is optional in the three-part chain, which a resolver has to know: `Lib.Member` and `Lib.Enum.Member` are different lookups.

A user enum reached through a library qualifier - deliberate nonsense, to bound how general the chain is. Predicting illegal. Its value is entirely in showing the first slot is not a free-form namespace.
